subject: Temporary headroom pools & autoscale surcharge discussion
messages:
From: Priya Desai <priya@scalegrid.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@scalegrid.com, amit@scalegrid.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Q: temporary headroom pools for holiday peak (Black Fri prep)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the dedicated pools look promising. We have a question as we prepare our Black Friday run: our traffic model shows a potential ~7x burst over baseline for a 36-hour window.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provide a short-term headroom pool (temporary additional GPUs) that sits above our reserved commit? We want capacity that can be used for a narrow window without permanently increasing our commit.
- How do you price that headroom? Specifically: is there a flat surge surcharge, per-minute billing, or a blended top-up rate? Any cooldown windows after a burst?

Attached is our rough demand forecast so you can see the shape. We also need to know whether using the headroom would affect our latency SLA and whether there are credits if we exceed committed throughput due to a platform issue.

Appreciate a quick outline — procurement needs a recommendation by Wednesday EOD.

Best,
Priya Desai
Head of Cloud Ops
ScaleGrid Solutions
[Attachment: ScaleGrid_Demand_Forecast_Q4.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya@scalegrid.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q: temporary headroom pools for holiday peak (Black Fri prep)

Hi Priya — thanks for the forecast, that helps a lot. High level answers below; I'll follow up with a one-page commercial sketch and an illustrative cost table by EOD.

1) Temporary headroom pools: yes — we can provision an isolated headroom pool (named "temporary headroom") tied to your Dedicated account for the requested window. The pool uses the same model variants as your reserved capacity and is isolated at the tenant level so it does not impact other customers.

2) Pricing options (we recommend Option B for ScaleGrid):
   - Option A (per-minute top-up): charged per GPU-minute at a premium multiplier (x2.5 of the committed per-minute rate). Good for very short spikes but can be unpredictable for long tails.
   - Option B (headroom credit slabs): you buy a slab of burst credits (e.g., 100k token-equivalent credits) billed upfront at a discounted surcharge (x1.6 effective rate vs on-demand), unused credits expire after the window. Credits consume continuously during the headroom window and are drawn before per-minute top-up.
   - Option C (blended surge overlay): an hourly slab that caps the hourly effective rate; useful if you expect sustained elevated demand for multiple hours.

3) Cooldown and limits:
   - Cooldown: default 2-hour cooldown after a contiguous 6-hour burst to avoid repeated oscillation; can be shortened to 30 minutes for a higher surcharge or with pre-warmed reserved buffer (we can model this).
   - Per-request caps: we enforce a per-customer concurrency cap to protect the noisy-neighbor risk; can be raised for a defined window with advance notice.

4) SLA and credits: using the headroom pool does not void your latency SLA. If Redwood fails to meet the committed latency SLO due to platform degradation during your burst window, we provide incident credits per the SLA plus a pro-rated headroom credit refund for the affected window. Normal over-commit (you exceed expected usage) does not generate credits.

Recommended next steps:
- We draft a short amendment (1-page) that adds a temporary headroom SLA and credit slab with dates and an estimated credit size.
- You confirm whether Option B or C looks closer to what you want and the rough credit quantity.

Looping in Marissa (Commercial) and Karthik (Pricing) to outline the numbers.

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Dedicated Products
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Amit Rao <amit@scalegrid.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, procure@scalegrid.com
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q: temporary headroom pools for holiday peak (Black Fri prep)

Vivek / Marissa — quick procurement follow-up. A few clarifying points from our side after reviewing the options: 

1) If we choose Option B (headroom credit slabs) we need the ability to return unused credits within a 7-day grace period (at 80% refund) or roll them to the next quarter; this is a standard ask to avoid overbuying for unpredictable spikes.
2) For the cooldown: the default 2-hour cooldown would impact our auto-heal patterns. Can the cooldown be measured per-headroom-pool instance rather than per-account? That would allow us to bounce back on a separate pool.
3) If Redwood provides a pre-warm buffer (20% of expected peak) as a part of the headroom package, can that portion be discounted at committed rates?

Also attaching a redline from legal that adds a clause asking for a service credit if headroom provisioning is delayed more than 30 minutes for the first 6 hours of the window.

Thanks,
Amit
Director, Infrastructure
ScaleGrid Solutions
[Attachment: redline-draft-amendment-v1.pdf (PDF)]

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Amit Rao <amit@scalegrid.com>, Priya Desai <priya@scalegrid.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q: temporary headroom pools for holiday peak (Black Fri prep)

Hi Amit / Priya — thanks for the redlines and the pragmatic asks. Quick replies inline, then next steps below.

> 1) refund/roll policy for unused credits
We can offer: 80% refund within 7 days OR roll up to 50% of unused credits to the next quarter. If you want a larger roll-forward we can do that with a 5% surcharge on rolled credits.

> 2) cooldown measured per-headroom-pool instance
Yes — we can scope the headroom as an independently managed pool with its own cooldown window. That removes the interaction with your committed pool and will allow parallel auto-heal behavior.

> 3) pre-warm buffer at committed rates
We can pre-warm up to 20% of the estimated peak at an effective rate that matches your committed GPU-minute rate (no surcharge) provided you give 48 hours notice and sign the short amendment. The remainder of usage in the temporary pool will draw from the headroom credits or per-minute top-up (depending on which you purchase).

> provisioning delay credit
We will accept the 30-minute provisioning SLA for the first 6 hours and will add a clause for a pro-rated headroom credit refund if we miss that window. Ops note: provisioning guarantees are tied to regional capacity — a carve-out for force majeure will remain.

Summary commercial sketch (Option B, recommended):
- 200k token-equivalent headroom slab covering the 36-hour window
- Price: 1.6x committed rate (billed upfront; 80% refund in 7 days if unused OR roll up to 50% to next quarter)
- Pre-warm: 20% of expected peak at committed rate with 48h notice
- Cooldown: per-headroom-pool instance, default 2 hours, editable in amendment
- SLA: 30-minute provisioning for the first 6 hours; failure triggers pro-rated headroom credit refund

Next steps:
1) Vivek: please approve the wording and numbers so we can send an amendment PDF for signature. (I've drafted a one-page amendment in DocuSign.)
2) Karthik: please confirm final per-GPU-minute numbers and whether we can offer a 5% sticker discount for annual committed customers signing the amendment now.
3) Priya / Amit: if that sketch looks close, we'll convert to a short amendment and send the DocuSign link.

Thanks — will stand by for final sign-off.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference
